Notes: Earliest documented Jewish presence (basis for Year Established): Josephus (War 2.103-104; Ant. 17.328-329) says the pseudo-Alexander, a Sidonian Jew posing as Herod's executed son Alexander, landed at Dicaearchia (Puteoli) and received many gifts from the Jews of the place; persons who had been friends of Herod received him like a king. Lacerenza dates the episode c. 4 CE ('verso il 4 d.C.'; other reckonings put it shortly after Herod's death c. 4 BCE). Lacerenza notes the Puteolan Jewish community was described as better connected than those of Crete and Melos and included people close to the Herodian court (unclear whether settled or passing through). Suggests an established and fairly wealthy community; no figure given. No earlier Jewish presence documented.

c. summer 36 CE: Agrippa I sailed to Puteoli; the Alexandrian alabarch Alexander paid part of a loan in Alexandria and promised the balance on arrival at Dicaearchia (Josephus Ant. 18.159-161). Traditional interpretation (cited by Lacerenza): Alexander had an agent or banking branch at Puteoli; D. Schwartz disputes this. Lacerenza counts it among data on the Puteolan Jewish community but it is indirect and uncertain evidence of resident Jews. No figure.

c. 40 CE (Lacerenza also allows winter 38/39 or 39/40 for the embassy's arrival): Philo and the Alexandrian Jewish embassy (five elders of the Alexandrian gerousia - a delegation, not residents) lodged at Dicaearchia/Puteoli while following Gaius; a man Lacerenza identifies as a Puteolan Jew brought them news of Caligula's order to set up his statue in the Jerusalem Temple (Philo, Legatio 185-186; 190-206). Indicates resident Jews at Puteoli; no figure.

c. mid-1st c. CE (freedman of the Claudian or Neronian era, 41-68 CE; midpoint used): lost Latin inscription from Quarto Flegreo in Puteoli's territory (CIL X 1893; CIJ I 561; JIWE I 23): 'Ti. Claudius Philippus diaviu et gerusiarches maceriam duxit' - a gerusiarch (head of a Jewish council of elders) built a wall, probably enclosing a funerary area perhaps reserved for Jews. Points to an organized community with a gerousia; no figure.

c. 59 or 60/61 CE: Acts 28:13-14 - Paul, brought as a prisoner to Rome, found 'brethren' at Puteoli and stayed seven days. Lacerenza: probably Christians, more precisely Jewish co-religionists already acquainted with Christian teaching. Small group of Jesus-followers of likely Jewish background; no figure.

c. 63/64 CE: Josephus (Life 13-16) landed at Dicaearchia/Puteoli after shipwreck and there met Aliturus, a Jewish-born actor favoured by Nero, who introduced him to Poppaea. Lacerenza (following Applebaum 1976) thinks Aliturus' presence reflects the occasional presence of Nero's court rather than membership in the local Jewish community, so this is weak evidence of resident Jews. Not given a row: the epitaph of Claudia Aster, a captive from Jerusalem (CIL X 1971; JIWE I 26), from Puteoli's territory, dated end of 1st c. CE (c. 70-95) - after the period limit.
